messages:
nina: saw a sharp p99 tail on host preparse around 01:12 UTC after the new kernel rollout. p99 +58ms vs baseline. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/4343210000 :boom:

infra-bot: alert: host-preparse.p99 +58ms window=6m affected=host-runtime-21[ab]\n
omar: dumped a few CPU samples. top hotspots are in TokenEmitter::pad_align and then lots of tiny grpc writes. collapsed stack snippet:

```
# collapsed
TokenEmitter::pad_align  39.1ms
UnpackFrame::deserialize 18.6ms
grpc::writev             20.3ms
Reactor::poll             2.4ms
```

ben: the selector opted into a new 'vec-align-pro' kernel for seq <= 50 during rollout. that kernel pads every token to 32-byte boundaries with an extra memcpy for vector-friendly loads. great for long sequences but noisy when there are many small token emits.

tess: did the batching estimator get updated after the selector change? i.e., the estimator's kernel_cost table might be stale and now underestimates vec-align-pro cost, causing smaller batch targets and more batches (and more small writev syscalls).

omar: confirmed. rollout changed selector rules but the static cost matrix in config store was not refreshed. estimator treats vec-align-pro as cheap and reduces target_batch_size for short sequences. result: batch_count up, writev_count up, p99 up.

nina: quick local repro with microdriver:
```
$ ./micro --kernel=vec-align-pro --seq=40 --batch_hint=auto
p50 10ms p95 30ms p99 52ms
# scalar baseline p99 ~13ms
```

ben: short-term mitigation: add a runtime clamp so the estimator uses cost = max(current, scalar_cost) for any newly-introduced kernel until we finish rebench. i'll push a small gate change.

ops-bot: runtime flag available: runtime.kernel.force_scalar_for_shortseq. can flip per-cluster without restart.

tess: please enable on canary and also emit a per-request metric kernel_id for 12h so we can see how often selector picks vec-align-pro vs scalar. also enable grpc_writev_coalesce metric to track syscall counts.

omar: toggled flag on canary at 01:45 UTC (runtime.kernel.force_scalar_for_shortseq=true). adding kernel_id trace tag for 12h.

infra-bot: canary telemetry: host-preparse.p99 trending down ~45ms, grpc small write syscalls per request down ~62%. KV hit rate delta ~1.2% correlated with batch shrinkage but likely secondary.

nina: plan of record:
- ben: implement estimator clamp + update rollout script to refresh cost table entries for any new kernel (short)
- omar: run full rebench suite for vec-align-pro vs scalar across seq lengths [8,16,32,48,64] and batch sizes [8,16,32], capture memcpy bytes and syscall counts (short)
- tess: instrument estimator to surface chosen batch_target and reason in metrics for 24h (short)
- ops: run a KV-prefetch probe to measure miss amplification vs batch size (short)

ben: i'll also add a temporary ingress coalescer in the proxy that groups writev calls for up to 150us or until combined size > 1KiB. opt-in by backend. naive pseudocode pushed in CL:
```
buffer = []
start = now()
for frame in frames:
  buffer.append(frame)
  if sum_len(buffer) > 1024 or now()-start > 150us:
    grpc_writev(buffer)
    buffer.clear(); start = now()
```

tess: prefer feature-flagged rollouts for coalescer and a mem-pressure short-circuit (if mem_pressure>0.85 flush immediately). don't want to add buffering during GC/pressure.

omar: owners assigned: @ben clamp + rollout-script patch, @omar rebench & syscall traces, @tess estimator metrics + coalescer gating, @ops kv probe + canary flips. nina will coordinate postmortem after benches.

ops-bot: flag applied to canary for coalescer at 02:08 UTC (ingress.coalesce_writev_ms=0.15). emitting grpc.writev_coalesced_ratio.

nina: thanks team. we'll hold the selector rollout until rebench confirms vec-align-pro is net-positive and cost table is reconciled. will follow up with a short postmortem and update the rollout checklist to include cost-table refresh & small-write smoke test. :white_check_mark:
